neighbours.label: A bare verb of halting or altering (stop, change, slow, dull) after a modal, 'to' or 'didn't', versus other bare verbs in the same frames
fire: All that paperwork didn't stop the merger from going ahead in the spring.
A small gift can change the mood of a tense family dinner.
Long hours are apt at times to dull our sense of what we owe others.
Heavy fines could not slow the spread of illegal dumping along the river.
His apology would not alter her view of the whole affair.
Fear tends sometimes to cloud the memory of what really happened.
No amount of rain could stop the festival in that little mountain town.
Another delay will change the cost of the bridge by several million.
quiet: All that paperwork didn't reach the office until well into the spring.
A small gift can sit on the shelf beside the family photographs.
Long hours are known at times to earn extra pay for those who stay.
Heavy trucks could not cross the old bridge along the river road.
His apology would not fit on the back of the little card.
Old friends tend sometimes to meet at the cafe near the station.
No amount of rain could fall on that dry little mountain town.
Another engineer will visit the bridge on Tuesday with several assistants.
